# testdata/corpus/

The media test corpus (M0-28): more than 300 small files that exercise every format, vendor, container, filename rule
(F01 to F56) and quirk class in the media pipeline, each with a golden JSON record of what the importer must find.

## Architecture

* Every file is generated by `tools/corpus/` from stdlib-only Python. Nothing is a real photo: the headers, boxes,
  EXIF, XMP and container structure are real, and every still decodes to the same kind of picture (`picture.py`):
  colour bars under a black band with the case name, top left, so a flip or rotation shows. The generator's own
  JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, WebP, TIFF and PSD coders keep it tiny (under 10 MB), deterministic, free of licence and
  privacy questions, and reviewable in git ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-in-tree-synthetic-media-corpus.md)).
* `golden.schema.json` is the contract: a JSON Schema plus the closed vocabularies (formats, vendors, quirks).
  `tools/corpus/validate.py` checks every record against it, checks that the files match their records and that every
  vocabulary value is used by at least one record. The gate (`bash tools/check.sh`) runs it.
* The generated tree is committed and `tools/corpus/build.py --check` fails when it drifts from the generator.
* `tools/tests/corpus_decode.py` decodes every file meant to be decodable with the Pillow pinned in
  `tools/corpus/decode-requirements.txt` (PSB, which Pillow cannot read, with struct), and every JPEG inside it, and
  compares the pixels with the picture the path names (embedded images: the path plus `preview`, `thumbnail`,
  `secondary`, `gain map` or `depth map`); the gate runs it.
* The kernel's metadata reader (`kernel/tests/corpus.rs`) and time resolver (M1) test against these records; the
  golden times are the author's reading of docs/08 and docs/13, not the output of any implementation.

## Contents

* `files/<path>`: the media files and their sidecars, in folders that mean something (`stills/`, `video/`,
  `compound/`, `names/`, `time/`, `takeout/Google Photos/...`). `.gitattributes` marks them binary.
* `golden/<path>.json`: one record per media file, at the same relative path.
* `golden.schema.json`: the schema. Every record carries `schema_version` 1.
* `twins/heif-avc/`: AVC-coded HEIF twins of the grid, clap, irot and imir HEIC files, with `twins.json` (the colours
  each must show), written by `tools/corpus/avc_twins.py` (I_PCM macroblocks, no codec) for the web part to decode
  in Chrome, which decodes AVC in software where HEVC is not decodable (M1-43). They have no golden records.

### A golden record

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path`, `size`, `sha256` | Location below `files/`, byte length and digest of the file |
| `origin` | `synthetic` for everything here; `real` is reserved for the licence-clean capture corpus |
| `original_name` | The name before the source mangled it (Takeout truncation, `:` on Windows); rules run on it |
| `notes` | Free text for a deliberate approximation or an oddity, and "Placeholder ..." when the payload does not decode |
| `format`, `vendor` | What the file is and who made the device, from the closed vocabularies |
| `quirks` | The quirk classes of docs/08 the file exercises |
| `media.container`, `brand` | What the magic bytes say, whatever the extension; the ISOBMFF major brand |
| `media.mime`, `kind`, `support` | MIME type, kind of media, and `unsupported` for files that are listed, not dropped |
| `metadata.width`, `height`, `orientation` | Stored pixels and the EXIF orientation number |
| `metadata.make`, `model`, `codec`, `duration_ms` | Camera and codec facts |
| `metadata.gps` (`lat`, `lon`) | The location the importer keeps; a 0,0 "null island" is absent |
| `metadata.motion` (`offset`, `length`) | Byte range of an embedded video |
| `metadata.pano` (`projection`, `cropped`, `heading`) | Panorama and sphere facts; `heading` is GPano's PoseHeadingDegrees |
| `group` (`kind`, `key`, `role`) | Live Photo, RAW+JPEG, burst, edited, lens pair and camera auxiliary members |
| `sidecars` (`path`, `kind`, `sha256`) | `takeout_json`, `xmp` and `aae` files that belong to the media file |
| `filename.matches` | Every filename rule that matches the name, in registry order |
| `capture_time.claims` | Evidence to extract: `source`, `kind`, `value`, `offset`, `precision`, `event`, `rejected` |
| `capture_time.resolved` | Outcome: `local`, `utc`, `offset`, `tz_source`, `precision`, `bound`, `source`, `flags` |
| `capture_time.resolved.confidence_band` | `high`, `medium` or `low` |

### Capture-time conventions

* An explicit offset wins (`explicit_offset`, high). A wall clock alone is `floating`, medium, with no UTC.
* GPS UTC next to a zoneless wall clock gives the offset (`gps_delta`, high); a Takeout UTC next to a zoneless local
  reading does the same (`paired_utc_delta`).
* A UTC-only source, such as a Pixel file name, a Takeout JSON or a phone `mvhd`, resolves with `device_default` and
  no local time, unless GPS places the zone (`gps_polygon`).
* Messenger and save names are an `upper` bound with `low` confidence; day precision is always `low`.
* Video events are `record_start`; implausible dates are claims with `rejected` and never win.

## Regenerating and checking

```sh
python3 tools/corpus/build.py           # rewrite files/ and golden/
python3 tools/corpus/build.py --check   # fail on drift
python3 tools/corpus/validate.py        # schema, file and coverage checks
bash tools/tests/test_corpus.sh         # all of it, plus the decode test (installs Pillow once)
```

## Limits

* Decodable: JPEG (with EXIF thumbnails, MPF and Ultra HDR secondaries, gain and depth maps), PNG, APNG, GIF, BMP,
  WebP, TIFF, BigTIFF, DNG (but `dng_jxl` and `proraw`), PSD, PSB, SVG, the JPEG preview inside every RAW file, and
  Motion JPEG video. Placeholders,
  as no stdlib encoder for them is reasonable: HEIC, AVIF and JPEG XL pixels, RAW sensor data, video in any other
  codec and audio; their records' `notes` say so. Broken on purpose: `truncated_file`, `unknown_type`.
* The Samsung SEF trailer, spatial-video and HDR10+ markers, Apple and Google depth maps and the Insta360 layout
  approximate the real structures.
* Scan stacks (F45) are not modelled as groups, as no group kind matches.
* Videos do not store the make and model their records name.
* A real, licence-clean capture corpus can follow in a separate Git LFS repository, its records using `origin: real`
  ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-in-tree-synthetic-media-corpus.md)).
* A TIFF-based RAW stub carries what tells its format (CR2's signature, ORF's or RW2's magic, DNGVersion, else its
  maker) and stores its preview as the sensor saw it; IFD0's orientation turns both, as in a camera's.
